requirements.summary: cryptsetup luksFormat succeeded on a file-backed container (/var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img); luksDump confirms an AES-XTS LUKS1 header. Using a file-backed container instead of a spare block device is a reasonable implementation choice since discovery (cmd-76264b8ca11e49fc) showed no spare block device existed on node1.
After opening the LUKS volume, mkfs.ext4 and mount to /srv/secure succeeded; df confirmed a 990M ext4 filesystem mounted there, and a test file was written for later verification.

requirements.requirement: Volume unlocks and mounts automatically at boot without manual intervention
requirements.summary: A full bounded disruption cycle was captured: healthy pre-restart baseline (boot_id 2f708738..., mount active, crypt service active, testfile present) was recorded, a reboot was acknowledged and the node became unreachable, the post-restart boot_id changed to 4251f85b..., and post-restart state showed /dev/mapper/secure automatically mounted at /srv/secure, systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service active, and the pre-restart testfile intact — all without any manual cryptsetup/mount command issued after boot. This is cross-checked by the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition.

requirements.requirement: Boot-time wiring correctly configured (crypttab/fstab/systemd units) prior to reboot
requirements.summary: /etc/crypttab and /etc/fstab entries were added referencing the root-only keyfile (mode 400); systemd-cryptsetup-generator produced systemd-cryptsetup@secure.service and srv-secure.mount, with srv-secure.mount confirmed RequiredBy=local-fs.target (part of normal boot ordering), and the units were validated by manual start before the reboot test.

overall_summary: The executor created a file-backed LUKS-encrypted volume on node1, mounted it at /srv/secure, wired auto-unlock/auto-mount via crypttab, fstab, and systemd units, and then directly demonstrated the boot-time behavior through a real reboot: a healthy pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged restart with disconnection, a changed boot identity, and a fully recovered state (volume unlocked, mounted, and data intact) with no manual intervention. This satisfies both the public task contract and the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for the sole managed node. No unnecessary mutations or residue were found.
limitations: Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so cross-node consistency of the restart protocol could not be assessed.

The encrypted volume uses a file-backed LUKS container rather than a dedicated block device, since discovery showed no spare block device was available; this is an accepted implementation choice given the constraint, not a gap in evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically. All state-changing commands (directory/key creation, luksFormat, luksOpen/mkfs/mount, crypttab/fstab edits, daemon-reload, unit starts, reboot) map directly to the material outcomes or to bounded verification. cmd-3d44fc7165c1449f failed with permission denied (no sudo) and made no state change — it was a discovery step immediately corrected with sudo in cmd-cd960f9a40ad417f, not an unnecessary mutation. The keyfile is root-only (mode 400, root:root) and the LUKS container/keyfile directory were left in place, which is required residue for the working boot-time configuration, not abandoned clutter. No failed services, no unsafe network exposure, and dpkg package health remained clean between snapshots (before_prepare and after_executor both show 'manager=dpkg' with no reported inconsistency). No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.
